claims.text: The proposed material is a composite comprising a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix and embedded WS2 nanosheets.
Optimizing bonding between WS2 nanosheets and the refractory high-entropy alloy matrix will improve self-lubricating performance across a wide temperature range.
Optimizing the WS2–matrix interface will maintain the composite's mechanical strength.
A controlled deposition or coating technique can enhance bonding between WS2 nanosheets and the alloy matrix.
A strengthened, coherent WS2–matrix interface facilitates effective stress transfer.
A strengthened, coherent interface preserves the WS2 lubricating phase.
Enhanced interfacial bonding prevents delamination of WS2 layers under thermal and mechanical stress.
Enhanced interfacial bonding prevents degradation of WS2 layers under thermal and mechanical stress.
Preserving the WS2 layers maintains low friction through effective lubrication.
Enhanced interfacial bonding preserves the mechanical integrity of the refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
The interface-engineered composite will have a lower friction coefficient than a conventionally mixed composite.
The interface-engineered composite will have a lower wear rate than a conventionally mixed composite.
The reductions in friction and wear will occur without sacrificing mechanical strength.
Conventional incorporation of unmodified WS2 typically results in higher friction under extreme conditions because of poor interfacial bonding.
Conventional incorporation of unmodified WS2 typically results in higher wear under extreme conditions because of poor interfacial bonding.
Defects introduced by the deposition process may reduce the anticipated benefits.
Interface degradation during prolonged thermal cycling may reduce the anticipated benefits.
Failure to treat the interface uniformly at scale may reduce the anticipated benefits.
The magnitude of performance improvement depends on the precision of the deposition process.
The magnitude of performance improvement depends on long-term interface stability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
